To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fragmentation function of a heavy quarks is suppressed at small angles, and this suppression is due to the fact that the heavy quark is a slow moving particle.

the QCD jet from a heavy quark is suppressed relative to the jet from a light quark by the dead cone effect, the suppression is logarithmic in the ratio EQ/MQ and the suppression is maximal in the direction of the quark motion (the cone axis).

(1) The fragmentation function of the Q-quark is suppressed by the factor of Theta 0 at small x and is enhanced by the same factor at large x; (2) The fragmentation function is suppressed by the same factor Theta 0 in the region of the large transverse momentum; (3) The fragmentation function has a singularity at x=Theta 0; (4) The fragmentation function at large x is enhanced by a factor of Theta 1/Theta 0
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points: (1) the QCD fragmentation function for the Q-quark jet; (2) the QCD jet structure function; and (3) the QCD structure function.
the following problems: the QCD jet production by Q-quark, the dead cone and its influence on QCD processes, and the QCD jet fragmentation in the dead cone region.
the following questions: 1) What is the effect of the dead cone? 2) How is it connected with the QCD evolution equations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dead cone effect is a real QCD phenomenon, but its magnitude is strongly suppressed by logarithmic corrections.
the dead cone effect exists and is large enough to be observable, but it is difficult to estimate its magnitude.

the Q-quark fragmentation is characterized by the following specific properties: (a) the Q-quark jet contains a narrow cone of gluons of small transverse momentum (pT<<EQ) and of small emission angles (Theta 0<<1) which is the 'dead cone' region; (b) the Q-quarks do not produce the collinear gluons with the emission angles Theta 0>>1; (c) the Q-quar fragmentation is characterized by a small effective mass
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dead-cone effect is a consequence of the QCD dynamics and is not related to the Q-quark mass itself.
the dead-cone effect is a consequence of the kinematical restrictions of the QCD radiation in the Q-quark rest frame and it is not a consequence of the Q-quark spin or of the QCD dynamics.
the Q-jet is softer, wider and less collimated than the light q-jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCD radiation from the heavy quark is suppressed by the factor of (EQ/MQ)2.
the QCD radiation pattern of Q jets differs significantly from that of light jets, and the differences are not only due to the dead-cone effect, but also to the QCD radiation of a heavy quarks.

the QCD fragmentation of Q-quark is suppressed by the factor of Theta 0 at all scales, i.e. at the initial stage of jet evolution (Q 0 identical to EQ, Theta 0) and at the final one (Q identical to EQ, Lambda identical to Theta 0), as well as at all intermediate stages (EQ<<Q<<EQ, Theta 0<<Q/EQ<<1).
